title: st.login regression on streamlit 1.58.0 (streamlit cloud) - "Missing provider for OAuth callback"
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After upgrading from Streamlit **1.56.0 → 1.58.0**, `st.login()` fails on Streamlit Cloud with the following log messages:

```
Missing provider for OAuth callback; this often indicates a stale or replayed
callback (for example, from browser back/forward navigation).
```

The app works correctly on a local machine with identical code and secrets. 

Rolling back to **1.56.0 + Authlib 1.6.11** resolves the issue on Streamlit Cloud entirely.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if not st.user.is_logged_in:
    if st.button("Log in"):
        st.login()
else:
    if st.button("Log out"):
        st.logout()
    st.write(f"Hello, {st.user.name}!")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Attempt to log in via the OAuth provider
2. Observe "Missing provider for OAuth callback" in app logs; login fails

### Expected Behavior

OAuth login completes successfully, as it did on 1.56.0.

### Current Behavior

Login fails with `Missing provider for OAuth callback`. The error is consistent
and reproducible on Community Cloud but never occurs locally (secrets.toml is identical on Streamlit Cloud and local machine except for redirect_uri).

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0 (regression from 1.56.0)
- Python version: 3.13
- Authlib version: 1.6
- Deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud 
- OAuth provider: Google Identity
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15455)

### Analysis

This is a reproducible `st.login` regression between 1.56.0 → 1.58.0 that manifests only on Streamlit Community Cloud (works locally with identical config). The warning `Missing provider for OAuth callback` originates in `_auth_callback()` in [`lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py) and is emitted when `_get_provider_by_state()` fails to find an entry of the form `_state_{provider}_{state_code}` in `request.session` that matches the `state` query parameter returned by the OAuth provider.

The likely root cause is the same class of regression introduced when 1.57.0 made Starlette the default server and removed Tornado (PR #14553): OAuth state is now carried in the Starlette signed session cookie (via `SessionMiddleware`) rather than via Tornado's signed cookie infrastructure or an in-memory cache. If the session cookie is not delivered to `/oauth2callback` (e.g., dropped due to a `SameSite`/cross-origin redirect, stale chunked cookies from the pre-Starlette format on the Community Cloud subdomain, cookie size, or being routed to a different replica with a rotated cookie secret), the state lookup fails and we hit this exact log line. A previous instance of this pattern (`MismatchingStateError`) was fixed in #15048, and a very recent follow-up to actively clear stale/invalid auth cookies landed in #15420 (Jun 5, 2026) — this fix is post-1.58.0 and may already address the reporter's case once released; otherwise the residual Community-Cloud-specific failure should be debugged from there.

The reporter's mitigation of pinning `streamlit==1.56.0 + Authlib==1.6.11` is consistent with this being a Starlette-auth migration regression rather than a user-config issue.

### Related Issues

- [#14991](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14991) — *OAuth MismatchingStateError regression in 1.57.0 (works in 1.56.0)*. Closed; same Starlette-auth migration regression family (OAuth state lookup failing on cloud deployments), fixed in #15048 by moving state into the session cookie. The 1.58.0 symptom reported here is the next-layer failure mode (session present/absent vs. state mismatch).
- [#15407](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15407) — *App conversion tornado to starlette breaks page, when logged in*. Closed; covers stale Tornado-era `_streamlit_user` cookies surviving across the 1.56→1.58 upgrade and breaking the new Starlette auth flow. Fix in #15420 explicitly clears legacy root-path / invalid auth cookies during login — directly relevant to anyone whose users had logged in on 1.56.0 before the Community Cloud upgrade.
- [#13773](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13773) — *Google Auth does not work with multiple replicas*. Open; related shared-failure mode where the OAuth round-trip is split across hosts/replicas and cookies/state don't survive, which can produce the same "missing provider" signature on multi-instance deployments like Community Cloud.

Thanks for reporting this. I reproduced it on the latest main branch. The root cause looks like a missing bounds check in the iteration logic. Would be great to see this addressed.

Good news. This should just requires a change in Community Cloud because we filter cookies that are not specified. With our change to Starlette the OAuth state cookie gets lost. I am working on getting it changed, and I expect it to be fixed this week.

Hey [USER] I believe the change is now on Community Cloud and should work for you. Let me know if you see otherwise. Going to close this issue for now, but I will continue to monitor this over the next week in case you see any issues.
